**Verdict: PASS for DG4 round 9 (code-security-reviewer), with no new findings.** The candidate is `sha256:18c18fe4…d76c` (1475 files, source `f2ae717`, freeze commit `01ad2e1`). All seven findings I closed in earlier rounds re-verify on the rewritten history.

**Candidate identity and records-only diff**
- `candidate.mjs` gives the expected ID in a complete clone at the freeze commit, at the source commit and in the repository tree. HEAD stayed at `01ad2e1` for the whole run.
- The diff from `5cd1e06` (round 8's source after the rewrite) to `f2ae717` touches only `docs/delivery/**`. Outside `docs/delivery`, the old round-8 source `8553323` and `f2ae717` are byte-identical, so the product is the same code I reviewed in full in round 7.

**The history rewrite (D-136)**
- Old head to new head adds exactly 33 files, all additions, and they match `restored-paths.txt`.
- Each restored file has its original content: absent at the commit that deleted it, identical to the version just before.
- I checked all 360 lines of the old→new commit map, not just a sample. Subjects, authors, committers and dates are identical, and each pair differs only in restored run files.
- The rewrite starts after the DG3 gate commit `bc8f455`, so DG0–DG3 are untouched.
- The validator's write-once check reports 0 errors on the new head and 99 on the old head, exactly as D-136 states.
- I judge D-136 sound:
  - the `frozen_at` correction (B4) holds: all 9 rounds now equal their manifests, where rounds 3–8 had been 10–36 s off;
  - the `fix_revision` remapping (B2) holds;
  - `tools/gates` is unchanged, so no gate rule was weakened.
- One observation, not a defect: the backup ref is local-only, so a fresh clone of the remote cannot resolve old commit ids named in earlier records. D-136 discloses this and D-035 covers it.

**Re-verified findings (all now PASS → CLOSED_VERIFIED)**

| Finding | Severity | Re-run this round |
|---|---|---|
| F-DG4-100 | Medium | probe D, 4/4 |
| F-DG4-101 | Medium, mandatory | probe F rev2, 10/10 |
| F-DG4-102 | Low | web-cycle probe: 1 pre-DG4 cycle; the control at the old round-1 code still shows the 2 P4 cycles |
| F-DG4-103 | Low | probe C rev2, 6/6 |
| F-DG4-104 | Medium | all four validators pass |
| F-DG4-105 | Medium | probe GC rev2, 2/2 |
| F-DG4-106 | Low | the three fixed session test files, 80/80 on Node 22 and Node 24 |

For each one:
- every fix commit is an ancestor of `f2ae717`;
- its product diff is identical before and after the rewrite;
- the fix is still in the candidate at the file and line cited in the sidecar.

**Run this round, all exit 0**
- The validators: `--historical` for DG3, DG2 and DG1, `--register DG4` and `--pipeline`.
- Offline install, `pnpm -r build`, `typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`, `openapi:lint` (652 operations) and `check:no-cdn`.

**Not re-run this round (carried forward from round 7 on identical code)**
- The load envelope keeps code-security off the full `pnpm test`, the integration suite and e2e while qa runs them. Every carried-forward check says so plainly in the record.
- The round-7 runs carried forward include:
  - `pnpm test` on Node 22 and 24, including the disclosed Node 22 run that exited 1 on two raid tests timing out under load (the accepted F-DG4-148 class);
  - the integration suite twice;
  - the 766-call authorization sweep and the IDOR/scope probes;
  - the decimal and migration scans, the exactly-once suites and the static graph scans.

**Disclosed:** my first rewrite-check run printed 33 false MISMATCH lines because of a bug in my own script. I fixed it and re-ran; the committed log is from the fixed run, and the record explains this. The only warnings in my logs are the expected ones: the pre-build `mth-db` bin warnings during install, Vite's chunk-size advisory, and the lint flag `--max-warnings=0`.

- `docs/delivery/reviews/DG4/round-9/code-security-reviewer.verifications.json`
